chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Sa'd ibn al-Munthir ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) gave a sermon. (And others have reported it with a different chain, mentioning that he gave the sermon at Dhi Qar).

So he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'As for what follows, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with the truth to bring His servants from the worship of His servants to the worship of Him, and from the covenants of His servants to His Covenant, and from the obedience of His servants to His obedience, and from the guardianship of His servants to His guardianship, as a bearer of good news and a warner, and a caller to Allah by His permission, and an illuminating lamp.'

A return and a beginning, an excuse and a warning, with a judgment that He detailed, and a clarification that He perfected, and a Criterion that He distinguished, and a Quran that He made clear, so that the servants may know their Lord when they were ignorant of Him, and acknowledge Him when they denied Him, and establish Him after they had rejected Him.

So He manifested to them, Exalted is He, in His Book without them having seen Him. So He showed them His forbearance, how He forbore, and showed them His pardon, how He pardoned, and showed them His power, how He is powerful, and frightened them from His authority, and how He created what He created from the signs, and how He destroyed whom He destroyed from the disobedient by the examples, and reaped whom He reaped by the retributions, and how He provided, guided, and gave. And He showed them His judgment, how He judged, and was patient until He heard what He heard and saw. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with that.

Then, indeed, an era will come upon you after me, in which there is nothing more hidden than the truth, nor anything more apparent than falsehood, nor more numerous than lies against Allah the Exalted and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). And in that era, there is no commodity more worthless than the Book when it is recited as it deserves, nor any commodity more worthy of sale and more expensive in price than the Book when it is altered from its places.

And there is nothing among the servants or in the lands that is more rejected than the known good, nor more recognized than the evil. And there is no immorality more rejected, nor worse punishment than for the guidance in the presence of misguidance in that era. So the bearers of the Book cast it aside, and its memorizers forgot it, until desires overwhelmed them, and they inherited that from their fathers, and acted with the alteration of the Book, lying and rejecting. So they sold it for a cheap price, and they were among the ascetics.

So the Book and the People of the Book in that era are two castaway fugitives, and two accompanying companions in one road, not finding any protector for them. How good are those two companions, for them and for what they do for Him. So the Book and the People of the Book in that era are among the people, but not of them, and with them, but not truly with them. And that is because misguidance does not coincide with guidance.

And if they meet, and the people have met upon sectarianism and separated from the group. They have given their affair and the affair of their religion to one who acts among them with cunning, evil, bribery, and killing, as if they are the Imams of the Book, yet the Book is not their Imam. There remains with them from the truth only its name, and they do not recognize from the Book except its script and its diacritical marks.

The entrant enters for what he hears of the wisdoms of the Quran, but he is not satisfied sitting until he exits from the religion. He transfers from the religion of a king to the religion of a king, and from the guardianship of a king to the guardianship of a king, and from the obedience of a king to the obedience of a king, and from the covenant of a king to the covenant of a king. So Allah the Exalted lured them from where they do not know.

And indeed His snare is firm with hope and expectation, until they gave birth to disobedience among themselves, and submitted to tyranny. And the Book did not spare them from anything; they are straying and lost, having submitted to a religion other than the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and worshipped other than Allah.

Their mosques in that era are built up with misguidance and ruined from guidance. The guidance has been changed in them, so their reciters and their builders are the most failed of the creatures of Allah and His creation. From their presence misguidance flows and returns to them. So presence in their mosques and walking to them is disbelief in Allah the Magnificent, except for one who walks to them while knowing their misguidance.

So their mosques, due to their actions in that manner, became ruined from guidance and built up with misguidance. The Sunnah of Allah has been changed and His limits transgressed. And they do not call to guidance, nor distribute the booty, nor fulfill their obligations. They call the one killed among them on that basis a martyr, having come to Allah with fabrication and denial.

And they became self-sufficient in knowledge through ignorance. And before that, they mutilated the righteous with every mutilation, and named their truthfulness to Allah as a lie, and placed the bad punishment in the good deed.

And indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sent to you a Messenger from among yourselves, for whom your suffering is hard, who is eager for you, merciful to the believers (peace be upon him and his family). And He revealed to him a Mighty Book: 'Falsehood shall not come to it from before it nor from behind it; a revelation from the Wise, the Praised One.' An Arabic Quran without any crookedness, to warn whoever is alive, and to make the word true against the disbelievers.

So do not let your hopes distract you, nor let the term of life be prolonged for you. Indeed, those who were before you were destroyed by the length of their hope and the covering of their deadlines, until the Promised came upon them, from which the excuse is repelled and repentance is raised, and with it the calamity and retribution descend.

And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has conveyed to you with the Promise, and detailed for you the speech, and taught you the Sunnah, and explained for you the paths, to remove the cause, and urged upon remembrance, and pointed to salvation.

And indeed, whoever acts sincerely for Allah and takes His word as evidence, He guides him to that which is most upright, and grants him success to righteousness, and directs him and facilitates him to the best. For the neighbor of Allah is safe and protected, and His enemy is fearful and deceived. So be cautious of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, through frequent remembrance, and fear Him through piety, and draw near to Him through obedience, for He is Close and Responsive.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And when My servants ask you concerning Me, then surely I am very near; I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he calls on Me, so they should answer My call and believe in Me that they may walk in the right way.'

So respond to Allah and believe in Him, and magnify Allah. It does not befit one who knows the greatness of Allah to consider himself significant. For the elevation of those who know the greatness of Allah is that they humble themselves to Him, and the honor of those who know the majesty of Allah is that they submit to Him, and the safety of those who know the power of Allah is that they surrender to Him.

So they do not deny themselves after the limit of knowledge, nor do they go astray after guidance. So do not flee from the truth like the healthy flee from the one with scabies, and the healthy from the sick.

And know that you will not recognize guidance until you recognize the one who left it, and will not take the covenant of the Book until you recognize the one who broke it, and will not hold fast to it until you recognize the one who cast it aside, and will not recite the Book as it deserves until you recognize the one who altered it, and will not recognize misguidance until you recognize guidance, and will not recognize piety until you recognize the one who transgressed.

So when you know that, you will recognize the innovations and the pretense, and you will see the fabrication against Allah and His Messenger, and the alteration of His Book, and you will see how Allah guided whom He guided. So do not let those who do not know keep you ignorant. Indeed, the knowledge of the Quran is not known as to what it is except by one who has tasted its flavor.

So through knowledge, his ignorance was taught, and through it, his blindness was given sight, and through it, his deafness was given hearing, and he attained knowledge of what had passed, and revived after death. And he established the good deeds in the presence of Allah, Mighty is His remembrance, and erased the bad deeds through it, and attained pleasure from Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

So seek that from its people specifically, for they are specifically a light by which one is illuminated, and Imams to be followed. And they are the life of knowledge and the death of ignorance. They are the ones whose judgment informs you of their knowledge, and their silence informs you of their speech, and their outward informs you of their inward.

They do not oppose the religion, nor do they differ in it. For it is among them a truthful witness and a silent speaker. So they are, by their nature, witnesses to the truth and truthful reporters. They do not oppose the truth, nor do they differ in it.

The precedence has passed for them from Allah, and a true judgment has passed over them from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And in that is a reminder for those who remember. So grasp the truth when you hear it with a grasp of care, and do not grasp it with a grasp of narration. Indeed, the narrators of the Book are many, and its guardians are few. And Allah is the One Helped.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the era of misguidance regarding the Quran and its people according to the sermon of Amir al-Mu'minin?
ai.summary: This sermon, delivered at Dhi Qar, articulates the core Shia doctrine of *Tawhid* by contrasting divine servitude with human servitude, while prophesying a historical era of *Tahreef* (alteration) where the Quran becomes a commodity of the powerful. It establishes the epistemological necessity of knowing the specific individuals who preserved, neglected, and distorted the text to distinguish true guidance from misguidance. The narrative culminates in the identification of the Ahl al-Bayt as the living embodiment of the Quran, serving as the infallible interpreters through whom the Book's inner truth is accessed.
